key_insight: MAGIC learns task-specific multi-agent collaboration graphs by choosing, for each role, whether to use a single agent or a reusable group, enabling mixed-granularity organizations that better match subtask needs.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to design more efficient LLM agent systems, balancing performance with inference cost by adapting collaboration structure instead of using one fixed topology.
method: Sequentially construct the agent graph by selecting a functional role, instantiating it as an agent or group, and connecting it to existing units.
Optimize the construction policy with dense-reward reinforcement learning using trajectory returns from the current policy.
Use potential-based reward shaping from probe-based utility and structural signals to provide intermediate feedback while preserving the task reward.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MAGIC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across eight benchmarks and shows strong inference efficiency in an efficiency study.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on RL over a large combinatorial graph-construction space, training stability, reward design, and generalization across tasks may be challenging.
paper_title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
